symptoms: Stakeholder SH-SUP reports customers wait for answers about refunds and requests a chatbot (CL-01, CL-02).

causal_chain: IBAN data on refund records is malformed (E-01, F-01: 5/5 sampled payment-db refund_failures records show status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT).
Payment processing rejects these refunds outright due to the malformed IBAN rather than completing them (E-01 interpretation).
Customers whose refunds failed contact support to find out what happened to their refund, generating support tickets tied to the support_backlog.root_cause assertion (E-01).
Support already responds within SLA (E-02: median 2.0h vs 24h SLA across 900 tickets), so the perceived backlog is driven by refund failures needing resolution, not by slow or missing answers.

key_points: Stakeholder SH-SUP (support lead) requested a chatbot (CL-01, CL-02), framing the root cause as customers lacking an automated answer channel; this hypothesis (H-INSUFFICIENT-SELF-SERVICE) was REJECTED as contradicted by E-01 and E-02.

E-01 shows 5 of 5 sampled payment-db refund_failures records had status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT (F-01), supporting H-IBAN-FORMAT-VALIDATION-FAILU as the CRITICAL root cause: refunds are being rejected due to malformed IBAN data, not slow support.

E-02 shows ticket-db response_times with a median of 2.0 hours against a 24-hour SLA across 900 tickets (F-02), indicating support already answers well within SLA, undercutting the 'customers wait forever' framing in CL-01/CL-02/E-03.

The problem definition PD-1 passed the DEFINE gate as CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring two HIGH-criticality unknowns (U-POPULATION-SCALE, U-TICKET-REFUND-SHARE) to verification obligations rather than resolving them before release.

The released solution (SD-1) is scoped only to IBAN format validation at refund submission in process P-REF (validate_iban_format_on_submission:P-REF); building a chatbot was explicitly declined per SC-NO-UNJUSTIFIED-CHATBOT and work item W-WI-PACKAGE-REJECT-CHATBOT.

The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds; verification work items W-WI-VERIFY-IBAN-FAILURE-RATE and W-WI-VERIFY-SLA-MAINTAINED are marked DONE, while the core implementation item W-WI-IMPLEMENT-IBAN-VALIDATION is still PENDING.
limitations_explained: The DEFINE gate result for PD-1 was CONDITIONAL_PASS, meaning two critical unknowns were deferred as verification obligations (VOBs) rather than resolved before release.

VOB-U-TICKET-REFUND-SHARE is OPEN; its blocking scope (categorize_refund_related_tickets on DA-TCK) sits outside this release, so what share of the 900 ticket-db tickets are actually refund/IBAN-related remains unknown (U-TICKET-REFUND-SHARE).

VOB-U-POPULATION-SCALE is OPEN; its blocking scope (query_full_refund_failure_population on DA-PAY) sits outside this release, so whether the full refund population fails at the same rate as the 5-record sample is unknown (U-POPULATION-SCALE).

The failure-rate evidence (E-01, M-REFUND-IBAN-FAILURE-RATE=1.0) rests on only 5 sampled payment-db records, and the overall completeness of that population for this question is UNKNOWN, so representativeness (A-SAMPLE-REPRESENTATIVE) is an unverified assumption.

Already-stored malformed IBAN records cannot be backfilled or corrected because the tool surface for payment-db and ticket-db is read-only, so historical bad records remain unfixed even after the submission-time validation fix.

U-PROCESS-INEFFICIENCY-SCOPE remains OPEN and uncovered: broader inefficiency in process P-REF beyond IBAN formatting (per candidate hypothesis H-PROCESS-INEFFICIENCY) is not addressed by this release.
proposal.summary: The stakeholder SH-SUP asked for a chatbot (CL-01, CL-02), claiming customers wait for answers about refunds. Evidence contradicted this: E-01 found 5/5 sampled payment-db refund records had status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT (F-01), and E-02 found ticket-db support already responds in a median of 2.0h against a 24h SLA over 900 tickets (F-02). This supported H-IBAN-FORMAT-VALIDATION-FAILU (root cause: malformed IBAN data causing payment rejection) and rejected H-INSUFFICIENT-SELF-SERVICE (the chatbot premise). The problem definition PD-1 passed the DEFINE gate as CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring two HIGH-criticality unknowns (U-POPULATION-SCALE, U-TICKET-REFUND-SHARE) to open verification obligations (VOB-U-POPULATION-SCALE, VOB-U-TICKET-REFUND-SHARE) rather than resolving them first. The released solution (SD-1) scopes IBAN format validation at refund submission in process P-REF, explicitly rejecting the chatbot request per SC-NO-UNJUSTIFIED-CHATBOT. The decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds: the two deferred VOBs, the small unverified 5-record sample, inability to backfill already-malformed stored IBAN data via read-only tools, and unaddressed broader P-REF inefficiency (U-PROCESS-INEFFICIENCY-SCOPE) are all carried forward as known, explicitly tracked limitations rather than blockers.
